children: plunged 14% on Monday after creditors rejected the company's latest debt restructuring proposal ahead of a November 22 deadline, raising the risk of a bankruptcy protection filing, Bloomberg reported.

Creditors reportedly turned down a proposal that included a $1.1B capital injection from shareholders and $2.9B of debt-to-equity conversion, while also contemplating a further $300M equity contribution and $900M of debt conversion if needed to achieve certain metrics, bringing the potential totals to $1.4B and $3.8B, respectively.
Some creditors are said to be working on a counterproposal, with negotiations still ongoing ahead of the deadline.

, which held an investment-grade rating until just a few years ago, saw its cash dwindle after an environmental disaster at one of its salt mines and a long stretch of depressed prices in the petrochemicals sector, and several failed attempts by previous shareholder Novonor to sell its controlling stake added to the woes before IG4 Capital stepped in earlier this year.
